title: Air-Fryer Chips
subtitle: Crispy homemade chips from the air fryer
excerpt: Floury potatoes cut into thick chips, tossed with a little oil and salt, and cooked in the air fryer until crisp on the outside and fluffy in the middle. Better than oven chips.

recipe.sourceNotes: Air-fryer chips use a fraction of the oil of deep-fried chips but produce a crisper, lighter result than oven chips because the circulating hot air reaches all surfaces simultaneously. The key steps are identical to good oven chips: rinse the cut chips in cold water to remove surface starch, dry them completely, and cook in a single layer with space for air to circulate. Soaking in cold water for 30 minutes before cooking improves the result further.

recipeTools.notes: A 4-litre or dual-drawer air fryer for 2 portions at once.

content.text: Dry the chips completely after rinsing: wet chips steam rather than crisp. Shake the basket every 8 minutes to ensure even colouring. For thicker chips, allow an extra 3 to 5 minutes. The chips are done when the outside is golden and a knife slides in easily.
Rinse the cut chips in cold water and soak for at least 15 minutes if time allows. Drain and pat completely dry with a clean tea towel or kitchen paper.
Preheat the air fryer to 190 C for 3 minutes. Toss the dry chips in the vegetable oil and season with salt.
Spread the chips in a single layer in the air fryer basket. Do not pile them up. Cook at 190 C for 20 to 25 minutes, shaking the basket every 8 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Season with a little extra salt immediately on coming out of the air fryer. Serve straight away.
